speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you are experiencing intense itching and developing red bumps on your thigh and other parts of your body. To help me identify the cause, have these lesions appeared suddenly, and are there any associated symptoms like fever, fatigue, or joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with intense itching of his right thigh region for the past few days. He also mentions the recent formation of ‘red bumps’ in the same area. The patient has recently attended a business conference in Miami. He has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes type 2, and hyperlipidemia. The patient’s medication regimen includes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He denies any history of smoking or drinking.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies (infestation).

Given the intense itching, "red bumps," and recent travel to a crowded environment like a conference, I need to confirm the distribution and timing of the rash. Please tell me: Are the bumps concentrated between your fingers, on your wrists, or in the genital area, and is the itching significantly worse at night?
